claim: Let \(T_n=L(K_n)\) be the triangular graph for \(n\ge3\), and let \(\mathcal N(T_n)\) be its Lovász neighborhood complex. For \(3\le n\le6\), the reduced mod-two homology of \(\mathcal N(T_n)\) is nonzero in exactly one degree: \(\widetilde H_1(\mathcal N(T_3);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2\), \(\widetilde H_1(\mathcal N(T_4);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2\), \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_5);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{11}\), and \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_6);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{91}\). At \(n=7\), mixed-dimensional homology appears for the first time: \(\widetilde H_3(\mathcal N(T_7);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{246}\) and \(\widetilde H_4(\mathcal N(T_7);\mathbf F_2)\cong\mathbf F_2^{7}\), with all other reduced mod-two homology groups zero.
integrity: The face sets and every simplicial boundary map are reconstructed from the graph definition and reduced exactly over \(\mathbf F_2\). The accepted statement is finite and exhaustive; auxiliary computations over other primes are not used as proof.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is only about mod-two homology for triangular graphs \(T_3\) through \(T_7\).
No integral torsion, homotopy-type, or \(n\ge8\) statement is claimed.
Literature noncoverage is bounded by the recorded searches and source inspections.
title: Mixed-dimensional mod-two neighborhood homology first appears at \(T_7\)
